source_words: This document provides three shoe size conversion tables covering the major shoe sizing systems (Mondopoint, European and United Kingdom), as well as China, Japan, the Republic of Korea and United States. The tables are based on measurement of foot length ...
notes: Verbatim. The abstract goes on: 'this being the logical starting point for any shoe size marking system' and names the tables: 'Table 1 — Adults' technical shoe size conversion; Table 2 — Adults' recommended shoe size marking (simplified); Table 3 — Children's size conversion.' ISO 19407:2023: Edition 1, Approved 6/22/2023, 8 pages, Replaces ISO/TS 19407:2015, Status Valid. Korea is new in 2023: the 2015 text (GOST R 57425-2017's scope) names China, Japan and the US only.

source_words: NOTE Due to the different ways in which each system has been developed and interpreted over many years without being formalized and the absence of solution to the problem of shoe size conversions, Tables 1 and 2 provide a guideline which can benefit the consumer.
correction: Wording only: the 2023 abstract says 'the absence of solution to the problem of shoe size conversions', not 'exact conversion'; the guideline sentence is verbatim. Say: no solution to the problem of shoe size conversions exists, so Tables 1 and 2 provide a guideline.
notes: A NOTE in the scope. The 2015 text as GOST R 57425-2017 renders it does say 'exact': 'не существует принципиального решения проблемы точных переводов размера обуви' (there is no fundamental solution to the problem of exact shoe-size conversions), and calls Tables 1 and 2 'an optimal compromise solution beneficial to the customer'. Either reading supports the ≈.

source_words: Настоящий стандарт модифицирован по отношению к международному документу ISO/TS 19407:2015 «Обувь. Определение размера. Перевод систем определения размера» (ISO/TS 19407:2015 «Footwear— Sizing — Conversion of sizing systems», MOD) путем изменения отдельных ссылок, которые в тексте выделены курсивом.
notes: Translation: 'This standard is modified with respect to the international document ISO/TS 19407:2015 (MOD) by changing individual references, which are set in italics in the text.' Next sentence: the deviations are made because it is expedient to use the referenced national standard instead of the referenced international document. 'Only' is the claim's word; the foreword names no other change. Approved by Rosstandart order of 23 March 2017 No. 181-st, in force 2018-01-01, first introduced; prepared from TK 412's own Russian translation of the English version. PDF re-downloaded (205,495 bytes): JBIG2 page scans with an OCR text layer, read with pdftotext -raw and checked on page images rendered with the Windows PDF API.

source_words: Система Мондопойнт определена в [1] и основана на длине стопы. Интервалы между смежными размерами, использующиеся в данной системе, приведены в [2] как 5 мм (группа 1) или 7,5 мм (группа 2), начиная с нуля. ... Япония иногда выражает размер в сантиметрах, а не в миллиметрах.
notes: Translation: 'The Mondopoint system is defined in [1] and based on foot length. The intervals between adjacent sizes used in this system are given in [2] as 5 mm (group 1) or 7.5 mm (group 2), starting from zero. ... Japan sometimes expresses the size in centimetres rather than millimetres.' [1] is ISO 9407, [2] DIN 66074-2:1975, so the steps are DIN's. Also: 10 mm intervals are usually called 'full' sizes and 5 mm 'half'; 7.5 mm is used mainly for special footwear; China and Japan use Mondopoint to denote length; a NOTE says 'CM' or 'CMS' usually means Mondopoint in centimetres, though sometimes it turns out to be last length.

source_words: b) Европейская система (EUR) (ранее известная как Paris Points, French или Continental) основана на интервале между смежными размерами 6,67 мм, начиная с нуля. Данную систему можно интерпретировать как основанную на длине обувной колодки или длине стопы, в зависимости от страны происхождения
notes: Translation: 'The European system (EUR) (formerly known as Paris Points, French or Continental) is based on an interval between adjacent sizes of 6.67 mm, starting from zero. This system can be interpreted as based on last length or foot length, depending on the country of origin, among which there are differences in shoe size marking (see note 2).'

source_words: c) Система Соединенного Королевства (UK) основана на интервале между смежными размерами 8,47 мм, начиная с 101,6 мм (4 дюйма, что соответствует 12 размеру системы). Первые 13 размеров считаются детскими, затем шкала снова начинается с размера 1 для больших размеров.
notes: Translation: 'The UK system is based on an interval between adjacent sizes of 8.47 mm, starting at 101.6 mm (4 inches, which corresponds to the system's size 12). The first 13 sizes are considered children's, then the scale starts again from size 1 for larger sizes. This system was originally developed from shoe or last length and then recalculated to foot length.' The Russian literally reads 'size 12'; the formula note reads '25 corresponds to 12 sizes plus 13 children's sizes, and 12 размер corresponds to 101.6 mm or 4 inches', i.e. 12 steps x 8.47 = 101.64 mm, so '4 in = 12 sizes' is the faithful reading. Checked on the page image.

source_words: Система США (US) основана на интервале между смежными размерами 8,47 мм, начиная с 99,5 мм (3 11/12 дюйма). … Однако в действительности система США соответствует непосредственно системе UK, но с добавлением произвольного сдвига размеров на один размер для мужской обуви и на два размера для женской.
notes: Translation: 'The US system is based on an interval of 8.47 mm, starting at 99.5 mm (3 11/12 inches). The first 13 sizes are children's, then the scale restarts at 1. However, in reality the US system corresponds directly to the UK system, but with an arbitrary shift of one size for men's footwear and two sizes for women's.' 3 11/12 in = 99.48 mm; the fraction is stacked on the page (read on the page image). Table 2 follows the shift in all 81 rows (US men = UK + 1, US women = UK + 2). The two descriptions differ: a 99.5 mm zero is 2.1 mm (a quarter size) below the UK's 101.6 mm, while the stated rule is a whole-size shift.

source_words: Взрослый размер UK рассчитывают по длине стопы. (l_f + 2·8,47)/8,47 − 25, где l_f — длина стопы, мм, 25 соответствует 12 размерам плюс 13 детских размеров, и 12 размер соответствует 101,6 мм или 4 дюйма.
notes: Translation: 'The adult UK size is calculated from foot length: (lf + 2·8.47)/8.47 − 25, where lf is foot length in mm, 25 corresponds to 12 sizes plus 13 children's sizes, and 12 sizes correspond to 101.6 mm or 4 inches.' Printed as a built-up fraction, then '− 25,'. The OCR layer garbles it ('/г+2-8,47 / 8,47 ” 25’'), so every term was read on the page image (PDF page 5, standard page 2).

source_words: Размер EUR рассчитывают по длине стопы (l_f + 2·6,67)/6,67.
notes: Translation: 'The EUR size is calculated from foot length: (lf + 2·6.67)/6.67.' A built-up fraction ending in a full stop; read on the page image.

source_words: В обоих случаях разность между длиной стопы и длиной обуви (или длиной обувной колодки) берут как эмпирически эквивалентную двум размерам (двум размерам UK или двум размерам EUR соответственно).
notes: Translation: 'In both cases the difference between foot length and shoe length (or last length) is taken as empirically equivalent to two sizes (two UK sizes or two EUR sizes respectively).' The NOTE after it: an approach used for the European system but not established by the standard takes a 5 % difference between foot and last length instead of two sizes; both give very similar conversions to Mondopoint and UK for sizes 38 to 46 but differ by about a European half size at the smallest and largest sizes.

source_words: Например, таблица 2 показывает, что размер 4 UK соответствует размеру 36,5 EUR, и размер 8 UK соответствует размеру 41,5 EUR, в то время как обувь, часто маркирована как 4 UK/37 EUR и 8 UK/42 EUR. В то же время, таблицы 1 и 2 приняты наиболее технически корректными.
notes: Translation: 'For example, Table 2 shows that size 4 UK corresponds to 36.5 EUR and size 8 UK to 41.5 EUR, while footwear is often marked as 4 UK/37 EUR and 8 UK/42 EUR. At the same time, Tables 1 and 2 are taken as the most technically correct.' (The claim says 'the more correct'.) The NOTE opens: some customers may be puzzled by the EUR/UK conversion and think the marked EUR size should be raised by 0.5 against the UK size. Table 2's UK grading holds UK 4 -> EUR 36.5 and UK 8 -> EUR 41.5 (checked on the page images).

notes: Both cells read on the page image (standard page 5). With the exact steps Mondo 215 gives EUR 34.25 and UK 2 gives EUR 33.75, both exact ties; the table rounds the first down and the second up. All 11 exact Mondopoint-graded EUR ties (215, 225 ... 315) go down; both exact UK-graded ties go up (UK 2 -> EUR 34; UK 14.5 -> Mondo 317.5 -> 320). Wikipedia's sentence (Shoe size, 'Size marking': 'When converted values require rounding, they are rounded to a larger shoe size rather than a smaller one, to increase comfort.') is uncited; the table rounds to nearest (88 of 162 non-US values below the formula). The standard's NOTE in 2.3 prefers marking a little larger than smaller ('желательно маркировать размер обуви с небольшим завышением, чем с занижением'), the likely root of Wikipedia's line, but Table 2 does not follow it.

source_words: BS ISO 9407:2019 Footwear sizing. Mondopoint system of sizing and marking. Current. Published: 31 Jul 2019 … ISO 9407 specifies a method of designation and marking of footwear size called Mondopoint … ISO 9407 is applicable to all types of footwear. … BS ISO 9407:2019 supersedes BS ISO 9407:1991
notes: Scope in full: '...called Mondopoint, based on defined measurements of the foot that the footwear is intended to fit.' The 1991 edition 'has been withdrawn'. The page also says: 'Some manufacturers express size in centimetres rather than millimetres (e.g., 26 in place of 260 or 26.5 in place of 265). Other manufacturers give size markings that relate to last length rather than the foot length. Neither of these expressions of size conforms to ISO 9407.' (bears on CM/JP sizes). correction: The lines are as quoted, but the claim leaves out the US's first-ranked 'pound'. By UTS #35 an entry without geq takes 1 unless it is the last ranked (then 0), so: US person mass is pound at 1 lb and over, pound-and-ounce only under 1 lb; GB stone-and-pound at 1 st and over, pound-and-ounce under 1 st; HK pound-and-ounce throughout; the world default kilogram (gram under 1 kg).
notes: units.xml lines 525-533 on main, under <unitPreferences category="mass" usage="person">, after 001 kilogram and 001 gram. Spec (tr35-info.md on main): 'For any element without a geq attribute, the implicit value is 0 if it is the last ranked unit and 1 otherwise.' So CLDR shows a US adult's weight in plain pounds, not pounds and ounces.
